DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Fibroma (likely with Meigs' Syndrome).

The normal CA-125 level makes epithelial ovarian cancer highly unlikely, and the absence of weight loss reduces the suspicion for malignancy. Given the benign blood work and the specific combination of an ovarian mass, ascites (increased girth), and shortness of breath (pleural effusion), this clinical picture is classic for Meigs' Syndrome. I am requesting images of the abdomen and chest to confirm the presence of ascites and pleural effusion before finalizing the plan.
